summary.intent: Add unit test coverage for `crates/fuse/src/journal_helpers.rs` (0% coverage), then assess coverage options for `read_ops.rs` and `write_ops.rs` which also have 0% patch coverage.
summary.outcome: No tests were written. After investigation, the user interrupted the `journal_helpers.rs` work to pivot to `read_ops.rs`/`write_ops.rs`. Once the fundamental blocker for those files was identified (private `ReplySender` trait in fuser), the user chose to defer all test work and log a GSD todo instead.

repo: GSD todos are stored as markdown files in `.planning/todos/pending/` with filename convention `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`.
The project vendors a copy of fuser but also lists fuser 0.16 from crates.io — the vendored copy is distinct; which one actually compiles for `crates/fuse` required lockfile inspection.

FUSE reply types (`ReplyEntry`, `ReplyAttr`, etc.) require `Reply::new(unique, sender)` where `sender: impl ReplySender`, but `ReplySender` is private to the fuser crate (`mod reply` is not `pub`), making it impossible to construct reply objects in unit tests without patching fuser.

code.finding: Contains `build_upload_journal_entry`, `build_mkdir_journal_entry`, `wrap_key_to_hex`, `generate_entry_id`, `current_unix_ms` — all pure/synchronous helpers that are unit-testable once a `CipherBoxFS` can be constructed in tests.

Every handler terminates with a `reply.xxx()` call consuming a concrete `fuser::Reply*` type. Cannot be unit-tested without access to `ReplySender` (private in fuser) or refactoring handlers into pure + shim layers.
Same reply-object constraint as read_ops.rs. Additionally, `handle_read` and `handle_open` perform blocking network polls, so even with a capturing sender they would hang/EIO in tests.

workflow: The fuser out-header encodes `error: i32` (little-endian) at bytes[4..8]: 0 = success, negative errno on error — useful for any future capturing-sender implementation.

Three viable paths for covering read/write_ops: (A) expose `ReplySender` from vendored fuser fork + capture-sender helper, (B) refactor handlers into pure+shim, (C) E2E via real FUSE mount. Option A was identified as lowest-touch.

friction: Significant investigation time spent confirming that `ReplySender` is private in fuser before concluding unit tests for read/write_ops are not feasible as-is.
Ambiguity between vendored fuser and crates.io fuser 0.16 required lockfile and source inspection to resolve which one actually compiles.
User interrupted the original `journal_helpers.rs` work mid-investigation to pivot scope, resetting progress.
